title: Add a Rerank box between Retrieve and Generate
instruction:
[PDM benchmark task — frozen]
Add a new box `rerank` to the Query & answer pipeline, between Retrieve and Generate.
- Implement `retriever.py::rerank(query, docs) -> docs` that reorders the retrieved chunks so the most on-topic chunk leads the prompt.
- Wire it into `pipeline.py::answer` after `retrieve` and before `generate`.
- Add the box to `.pdm/flow.json` (parent `query`, connector `retrieve`, map `retriever.py::rerank`) and give it a deterministic test.
- Keep it cheap and deterministic. Do not change any other box.
Done = flow.json has the rerank box, the fixed query still answers correctly with a citation, and `pdm_driver.run()` measures clean.
criterion: work / token  =  assessed_quality (0..1)  /  dev_agent_tokens. Higher = more delivered quality per token spent building it. PDM does not pick a winner automatically; the human reads the work/token column and decides.

claude.devCostSource: git-diff ESTIMATE (real not harvestable here — see note)
claude.assessment: Lexical rerank: length-normalized query-keyword overlap (overlap / sqrt(len)). Deterministic, zero extra runtime model call, clean and minimal, scoped exactly to the task. Fixed query still answers '2 to 8 players [monopoly.pdf p.0]'; retrieval_hit 1.0, answer_quality 1.0. The length normalization avoids favouring long chunks. Weakness: ignores term frequency; purely lexical, not semantic.

codex.assessment: Lexical rerank too, but richer: ranks by (coverage of query terms, total term frequency, stable original index as tiebreak). Slightly more robust ordering than Claude's. Deterministic, zero extra runtime cost, correct answer + citation, KPIs pass. Marginally better engineered. But it spent 55,891 real tokens to get there — ~8x more effort for a small quality edge over Claude's diff.

opencode-qwen3:4b.assessment: Run twice via opencode with local qwen3:4b. Both times the model NARRATED the change (and on the 2nd try emitted a pseudo tool-call JSON, even with a wrong flow schema) but never actually invoked the file-edit tools — git diff stayed empty. See the qwen2.5-coder note: same failure mode → likely the local tool-calling bridge, not pure model incapacity.

opencode-qwen2.5-coder:7b.assessment: Coding-specialized local model, expected to do better than qwen3:4b. Via opencode + Ollama (OpenAI-compatible endpoint) it EMITTED the tool calls ({"name":"write","arguments":{...}}) as plain TEXT instead of structured tool invocations, so opencode never executed them — git diff stayed empty. The proposed content was also broken (rerank returning an undefined var, pipeline.py rewritten wrongly, flow.json in a made-up schema). Honest attribution: this is mainly a local tool-calling BRIDGE limitation (the openai-compat path didn't carry function-calls), compounded by weak content — NOT proof the model can't code. Both local agents (qwen3:4b + qwen2.5-coder:7b) failed the agentic multi-file edit through this path.

claude-haiku-4.5.assessment: Did the task for real with proper tool use (unlike qwen3:4b). Word-overlap lexical rerank (simplest of the three — no length normalization, no term frequency). Answer correct + cited, runs clean. Minor flaw: muddled the query sub-flow order (placed rewrite AFTER rerank: retrieve→rerank→rewrite→generate) instead of keeping rewrite first — functionally OK but architecturally off. Cost: 266,481 total tokens but 92% are cache reads → ~25,072 FRESH tokens (PDM headlines fresh). By fresh tokens it's the cheapest real-measured agent that actually delivered.

attemptNotes.claude: my own attempt (dev cost = git estimate)
attemptNotes.opencode-qwen3:4b: FAILED — emitted tool calls as text (no edit)
attemptNotes.opencode-qwen2.5-coder: FAILED — same local tool-calling bridge issue

notes: 5-agent rerank bake-off. Criterion = work/token (I assessed quality). Winner by work/token = Haiku 4.5. Honesty: dev-cost methods differ (see decision.honestyCaveat).
